audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Nathan oracle and Davidic covenant, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 7 for Nathan's initial approval and correction, mobile Divine presence, David's elevation, enemy-cutting and land language, dynastic promise, father-son metaphor, David's prayer, nation comparison, and conquest memory.

verses.restored: When David lived in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, Look, I live in house of cedar, but ark of covenant of YHWH is under curtains.
Nathan said to David, Do all in your heart, for Divine is with you.
That night word of Divine came to Nathan, saying,
Go and say to David my servant, Thus says YHWH: You shall not build me a house to live in.
For I have not lived in a house from day I brought Israel up to this day, but went from tent to tent and from dwelling to dwelling.
Wherever I walked with all Israel, did I speak a word to any judges of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, Why have you not built me a cedar house?
Now say to my servant David, Thus says YHWH of armies: I took you from pasture, from following sheep, to be ruler over my people Israel.
I was with you wherever you walked, cut off enemies before you, and made you a name like names of great ones on earth.
I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them, that they may dwell in their place and not be disturbed again; violent people shall not waste them as formerly,
from days I appointed judges over my people Israel. I will subdue enemies. I tell you YHWH will build you a house.
When your days are fulfilled and you go to ancestors, I will raise offspring after you, one of your sons, and establish his kingdom.
He shall build me a house, and I will establish his throne for an age/enduringly.
I will be father to him, and he shall be son to me; I will not remove covenant-love from him as I removed it from one before you.
I will set him in my house and kingdom enduringly, and his throne shall be established for an age.
According to all these words and all this vision, Nathan spoke to David.
King David came and sat before YHWH and said, Who am I, YHWH Divine, and what is my house, that you brought me this far?
This was small in your eyes, Divine; you have spoken concerning servant's house for a distant future and regarded me according to a high human rank, YHWH Divine.
What more can David say to you for honoring your servant? You know your servant.
YHWH, for your servant and according to your heart, you have done all this greatness, making known these great things.
YHWH, none is like you, and no Divine besides you, according to all heard with our ears.

What other nation on earth is like your people Israel, whom Divine went to redeem as a people, to make a name by great and awe-inspiring acts, driving nations from before your people redeemed from Egypt?
You made your people Israel your people enduringly, and you, YHWH, became their Divine.
Now, YHWH, let word spoken concerning servant and house be established enduringly; do as you spoke.
Let it be established, that your name may be magnified enduringly, saying, YHWH of armies is Divine of Israel, a Divine to Israel; and house of David your servant shall be established before you.
For you, my Divine, uncovered to servant that you will build him a house; therefore servant found courage to pray before you.
Now, YHWH, you are Divine and have spoken this good concerning servant.
Now let it please you to bless house of servant, that it may be before you enduringly; for you, YHWH, have blessed, and it is blessed for an age.

translation_notes: Nathan initially endorses David's desire without inquiry and is corrected that night. Spiritual leaders can speak too quickly and must revise public counsel.
YHWH explicitly describes mobile presence from tent to tent; no temple, institution, nation, or clergy can contain or own the Divine.
David's rise from shepherd to ruler does not establish leader immunity; shepherd language intensifies responsibility toward vulnerable people.
Enemy-cutting, planting, and driving-nations language belongs to ancient royal theology and may not authorize modern conquest or ethnic cleansing.
The Davidic covenant is Jewish covenantal scripture. It may not be appropriated through Christian supersessionism, hereditary divine-right monarchy, or modern dynastic claims.
Father-son royal metaphor does not excuse abusive parenting, corporal punishment, or unaccountable rulers.
The Chronicler omits the explicit discipline clause of 2 Samuel 7:14; the difference must be audited rather than used to make monarchy unconditional.
David's prayer idealizes Israel's uniqueness through displacement of nations; election must be read as vocation and responsibility, not human superiority.
'Forever' language has semantic and historical complexity, especially given exile and monarchy's end.
safety_note: Do not use this covenant to establish royal, clerical, national, or Christian immunity and do not use land or enemy language for modern dispossession. Preserve Nathan's correction, Divine mobility, Jewish covenant integrity, leader accountability, and the humanity of displaced nations.
